finding: Impact order on one tick: sound at the impact point, then explosion effects stamped with the projectile's own time, then direct damage that stamps the victim, then splash on a later tick (src/projectile.cpp 1185-1389; src/combat.cpp 458-460). Adapt: stamp every hit effect with the server impact tick.

Screen shake is a 100-step curve started by five call sites with fixed lengths per event class (feature.cpp 524, structure.cpp 4879-4888, projectile.cpp 1209). First request wins and the start uses the call-time clock (display.cpp 255-258). Keep the class idea; fix the gate, the clock and the roll.

Droid death: five debris pieces carry 0.9 x the unit's motion, in owner colour, with one destruction effect and one explosion sound, all at the impact tick (src/droid.cpp 665-692; src/component.cpp 1077-1137). Keep as the death presentation.
Weapon recoil is a triangle envelope over 250 ms with peak at recoilValue/10 (src/droid.cpp 83, 1435-1440). Reuse the envelope as a creature weapon kick shared across families.

Electronic-warfare shiver: 200 ms, three random tilts drawn with rand() on each use, plus a sideways jitter on droids (src/projectile.h 46; src/display3ddef.h 38-39; src/projectile.cpp 1887). Fix: seed from object id and tick. Useful as a stagger look for status effects.
Sticky status rule: a plain hit does not overwrite an EMP-class hit stamp until it ends (src/combat.cpp 458). Keep for many-on-one status rules.
Shake toggle label promises shakes when things die, but no droid death calls shakeStart (src/keybind.cpp 2410). Fix: give droid death a small class, or relabel the toggle.

Catalogue feel data: data/base/stats/weapons.json has 109 entries; 81 carry a numeric recoilValue (10 to 250, median 25), each with explosion count, size and sound key. Keep these as per-weapon fields in our catalogue.

Gap: no hit stop, no knockback and no flash on the victim in this tree (grep over src). Look test: three clips at 375 wide, A sound and flash, B plus translation shake, C plus recoil kick (md section 5).

Combat is a 3-second round beat: swing and dodge start at round start, damage lands at round end, and a floor flag holds HP at 1 when set (src/engines/kotorbase/round.cpp 36-62; module.cpp 726-754; creature.cpp 867-876). PARTIAL: only the beat is here, with no hit stop, shake, flash or sound.
Death: the die animation plays once, then the dead pose is held (src/engines/kotorbase/creature.cpp 896-897; area.cpp 825-826). Keep the die-then-hold presentation for row 17.

Shake and impact exist only as schema names: 10 cutscene shake ids (src/aurora/gff4fields.h 634-643) and GDA shake and impact columns (src/aurora/gdaheaders.cpp). No reader in src; the values are game data not in the box.

Defects in the beat: no hit roll before damage (creature.cpp 861-880, dodge plays regardless); no range check at resolve (module.cpp 745-756); the beat reads the engine clock (round.cpp 41-73). Fix: roll before damage, re-check range, drive from the server tick.
Many-on-one idea (not in donor): three attackers on one shared beat with a stagger, so incoming swings are readable one after another. Look test: free timing vs shared beat at 375 wide.
